key_insight: Plant-on-a-Disc (POD) combines parallel root cultivation with controlled radial microflow, enabling non-invasive in situ study of how hydrodynamics and confinement jointly shape root behavior.
engineering_relevance: The POD architecture offers a low-cost, scalable phytofluidic platform for reproducible root phenotyping under physiologically relevant flow with minimal disturbance to adjacent samples.
method: PDMS device fabricated with a wire-drawing process to create radial microchannels feeding a central sump under an optical window.
Eight seedlings are cultured in parallel while bright-field, fluorescence, and Raman measurements are taken sequentially with one microscope objective.
Dimensionless transport analysis and finite-element modeling were used to verify balanced hydraulic resistance, creeping laminar flow, and convection-dominated transport.
evidence_signal: In Brassica seedlings, flow conditions produced faster root elongation, strong ROS accumulation, anisotropic cortical cell expansion, and Raman-detectable carotenoid signatures.
watch_item: The platform’s utility depends on maintaining uniform low-shear flow and precise alignment for multimodal optical access, which may be sensitive to fabrication variability.
paper_title: Plant-On-a-Disc (POD): A Phytofluidic platform enabling In Situ Root Analysis
